newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina probing Sevel directors over share issue.
newsitem.headline: Argentina probing Sevel directors over share issue.

text.p: Argentina's Securities Commission said Thursday it had begun a formal investigation into car maker Sevel Argentina SA and top corporate chiefs over alleged price manipulation in a 1992 share issue.

The Commission said it was investigating Francisco Macri, Jorge Blanco Villegas, Mauricio Macri and other directors at the time of the issue in June 1992. None of the men named were immediately available for comment.

The National Securities Commission said its investigations had led it to suspect that, "in the initial public offering of Sevel Argentina SA there was manipulation of the cut-off price via the introduction in the tender process of an offer financed by the sellers themselves."

The Commission said it was also investigating Argentina's Banco Medefin SA, Bahamas-based BM International Bank and Trust Company Limited, and British Virgin Island-based Lawton International Corporation in connection with the issue.
The commission said it had been assisted in its investigation by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Local newspapers reported last month that Mauricio Macri, head of the SOCMA group controlling Sevel, said French carmaker Peugeot was about to boost its stake in Sevel to give it control of the company.
